title: A gate re-run on its record commit starts over
what: When HEAD differs from a sha with a finished gate log only by relay's record commits (files under .relay/checks/), `relay gate` gates it from scratch. 28 Oct, wf_a74e8dbc-fb9, py-green: the gate of f8b4fee went red at 03:05:58; the runner died; the retry gated 44a45c8 ("relay: gate of f8b4fee") from scratch: 39.4 lane minutes and 13.8 slot minutes other lanes waited for, same 4 errors. The already-running case is handled (setup-dirty joined pid 37966); the just-finished case is not.
why: Waste that repeats on every runner death (principle 2); 12 gate runners died in 24-28 Oct.
failing_case: HEAD = the record commit of a finished red gate: `relay gate` runs the whole gate again.
pass_cases: HEAD = record commit of a finished gate: the old result is printed and its exit code returned in seconds, no slot taken.
HEAD = record commit plus any change outside .relay/checks/: a full gate.
A gate still running: joins it, as now.
